sizes.title: Sizes
sizes.desc: 47 components take a `size`, and 34 of them take the same three values. The prop is not really a question of how big something should look — it is a question of how much of the screen a control has earned, and whether a finger can still hit it. Both of those have numbers behind them.
sizes.scale_desc: 34 of the 47 accept `sm` / `md` / `lg`, and 40 of them default to `md`. That default is the answer unless something argues otherwise, and the argument should be about the control's role, not about how the screen looks with it. Three exceptions are deliberate: `Tag` defaults to `sm` because tags are read in groups, `Container` to `lg` because it sets the measure of a page, and `Title` to `xl` because it is the heading. Typography (`Text`, `Span`) uses a wider `xs`–`xl` scale, and `Container`, `QRCode` and `Splitter.Panel` take a number instead.
sizes.choose_title: Choosing between sm, md and lg
sizes.sm_when: The control is secondary to something else on the same row — a filter beside a table, a tag inside a cell, an action inside a list item.
sizes.sm_not: It is the only thing the user came to do. A small primary action reads as optional.
sizes.md_when: The default. The control stands on its own and the user is expected to act on it.
sizes.md_not: You are shrinking a row that is already crowded — that is what density is for.
sizes.lg_when: The control is the point of the screen, or a finger has to find it without looking — a submit button in a mobile footer, a single call to action.
sizes.lg_not: Several controls sit together. Everything large is the same as nothing large.
sizes.measured_desc: The heights come from `--wim-height-*`, and the density setting rewrites them. Both columns ship; neither is hypothetical.
sizes.tap_desc: WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, WCAG 2.2) asks for 24×24 CSS pixels. WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) asks for 44×44, which is also what Apple's guidance uses. Reading those against the table above gives three facts worth knowing before choosing a size.
sizes.tap_1: `md` misses the AAA target by 2 pixels
sizes.tap_1_desc: 42px against 44. The default size of most controls is just under the comfortable-thumb threshold. `lg` (48px) is the only size that clears it.
sizes.tap_2_desc: `lg` drops to 40px. A layout that relies on `lg` for reachability loses it the moment the app switches density, and no component can see that switch coming.
sizes.tap_3: Controls built on `xs` fall under the AA floor in compact
sizes.tap_3_desc: `Rating` sizes its stars from `--wim-height-xs` and `Slider` sets its whole height from it. That is 24px by default — exactly the AA minimum — and 20px under `compact`. Nothing measures this: axe does not check target size, and a screenshot of a smaller star looks fine.
sizes.density_title: Size and density are not the same lever
sizes.density_desc: `size` is a per-component statement about one control's importance. Density is an application-wide setting that rewrites every control at once. They compose — a `compact` `lg` button is still the largest thing on its row — but they are not interchangeable. Reaching for `size="sm"` to fit more rows moves a global decision into one component, where the next screen cannot inherit it and where the tap-target consequence is invisible to whoever set the density.
